outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a personal tracking dashboard meant to organize publicly available information for research purposes. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: AI infrastructure capex commitments, led by the hyperscalers
strongest.reason: cloud infrastructure spending hit an eight-year high last quarter, and reports show Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, and AWS are on track to invest over $500 billion combined in AI infrastructure this year, underpinning continued conviction in the buildout even as individual chip and cloud stocks sold off today

strongest.area: Cybersecurity, led by CrowdStrike and Zscaler
strongest.reason: both names drew fresh price-target increases and, in CrowdStrike's case, a reported $572 million institutional investment from Renaissance Technologies, with Wall Street commentary continuing to frame AI-driven threats as a durable spending tailwind for the sector

weakest.area: Chips & semiconductors broadly, led by Micron, AMD, TSMC, and ASML
weakest.reason: the sector sold off sharply as disappointing SK Hynix results and a renewed U.S.-Iran standoff over the Strait of Hormuz combined to unwind recent AI-chip-trade gains, with memory names hit hardest

weakest.area: Enterprise AI software, led by ServiceNow, Salesforce, and Palantir
weakest.reason: all three fell 2.5-4.7% again today, extending a months-long pattern where persistent fears that AI agents and coding tools will erode SaaS pricing power have outweighed generally solid underlying fundamentals

outlook.nextStep: The combination of multidecade-high bond yields, elevated oil prices, and an unresolved Iran-Strait of Hormuz standoff is the macro overhang worth watching most closely, since it's driving today's broad risk-off move across chips and growth names alike. The chip-sector pullback is probably worth a closer look for whether it's a buying-the-dip opportunity ahead of Nvidia's August 26 earnings or the start of a deeper correction, while the enterprise-software slide is better watched than acted on given how consistently the group has kept selling off despite improving analyst sentiment.

signals.title: Bond yields hit multidecade highs as Iran-Strait of Hormuz standoff drags on
signals.body: The 30-year Treasury yield touched its highest point in nearly two decades, and the 10-year remains near its highest levels since early 2025, as an extended U.S.-Iran standoff over the Strait of Hormuz kept oil prices elevated and fed inflation concerns. The Fed held rates at 3.50%-3.75% in July with three dissents favoring a hike, leaving the door open to a September move.
signals.focus: worth a closer look given how directly this combination of yields, oil, and geopolitical risk is driving today's broader selloff

signals.title: Semiconductor sector sells off sharply on SK Hynix miss and Iran-driven risk-off trading
signals.body: Chip stocks fell broadly, with Micron down roughly 7%, AMD and TSMC both down over 4%, and ASML down nearly 5%, as underwhelming SK Hynix results and renewed U.S.-Iran tensions triggered an unwind of recent AI-chip-trade gains. Nvidia's August 26 earnings report remains the sector's next major catalyst.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether this is routine profit-taking after a strong run or the start of a deeper pullback ahead of earnings season

signals.title: Hyperscaler AI capex commitments stay strong despite today's stock-level weakness
signals.body: Cloud infrastructure spending hit an eight-year high last quarter, and reports show Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, and AWS are on pace to invest more than $500 billion combined in AI infrastructure this year, with an increasing share directed at inference rather than training. This underscores continued institutional conviction in the buildout even as individual megacap and chip stocks sold off today.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at which infrastructure suppliers are best positioned to capture this spending independent of daily price swings

signals.title: Enterprise software extends its AI-disruption-driven slide
signals.body: ServiceNow, Salesforce, and Palantir all fell again today, continuing a months-long pattern where fears that AI agents and coding tools will erode SaaS pricing power have outweighed generally solid earnings and revenue growth across the group.
signals.focus: lower conviction right now given how persistent the selling has been despite repeated fundamentals-based pushback from bulls

signals.title: Cybersecurity draws fresh price-target hikes and institutional buying
signals.body: CrowdStrike received price-target increases to $230 from Wells Fargo and $235 from TD Cowen, along with a reported $572 million investment from Renaissance Technologies, while Zscaler rose on continued positive sector coverage. Commentary continues to frame rising AI-driven cyber threats as a durable spending tailwind for the group.
signals.focus: worth a closer look given the combination of institutional buying and repeated analyst upgrades, though shares have already run up significantly this year

signals.title: Bitcoin holds steady range as regulatory backdrop improves
signals.body: Bitcoin traded in a steady $64k-$64.9k range even as bond yields rose. Citi announced plans to launch institutional bitcoin custody through a new platform, and the SEC unveiled a new crypto-asset framework offering token issuers clearer fundraising exemptions and a tokenization safe harbor.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether the improving regulatory backdrop starts to translate into fresh institutional inflows

signals.title: Robotics names diverge as Teradyne extends gains and Ouster pulls back sharply
signals.body: Teradyne continued higher on AI- and robotics-driven semiconductor test-equipment demand even as the broader chip sector sold off, while Ouster gave back a large chunk of last week's gains. The broader robotics and automation group remains up roughly 17% over the past 12 months even amid this kind of day-to-day dispersion.
signals.focus: worth treating the group's daily swings as noise relative to the longer-term trend, given how much dispersion there is between individual names
